summary: This roadmap compares generic trianguline deformation spaces with completed double-flag incidence varieties, retaining character weights and both framings. It derives local normality, tangent bounds, companion criteria and local cycle identities, then develops the crystabelline deformation and higher-intertwining parameters used to recover Hodge filtrations. A separate local branch supplies the ordered-regular tangent and numerical noncriticality inputs to eigenvariety arguments.

nodes.title: Almost de Rham deformation groupoids
nodes.statement: For an almost de Rham E⊗B_dR representation W of rank n, X_W(A) is the groupoid of pairs (W_A,ι:W_A⊗_A E≅W), with equivariant isomorphisms compatible with ι. X_W^pdR adds an A⊗K-linear frame α_A:(A⊗K)^n≅D_pdR(W_A) lifting a fixed α. Pullback along A→B is tensor product, retaining the special-fibre identification.
hypotheses: K/Q_p is finite of degree d; E/Q_p is finite and contains every embedding Σ=Hom(K,E); n≥1. Art_E means local Artinian E-algebras with residue E and local E-maps inducing the identity on E. All actions and characters are continuous. Frobenius linearizations are invertible; Robba modules have the finite projectivity or freeness specified in each target.

BHS conventions: a labelled character weight is its logarithmic derivative, so the cyclotomic character has weight +1. The n Hodge–Tate–Sen weights at τ are ordered h_{τ,1}<⋯<h_{τ,n} when regularity is assumed. A D_pdR frame has dn² parameters, while a Galois frame has n².
W is finite free over E⊗B_dR. Almost de Rham, B_pdR, D_pdR and its nilpotent ν are imported from the requested PadicHodgeTheory Part II interface.
proofSteps: Use the coefficient Fontaine equivalence to show every Artinian deformation is almost de Rham.
Transport tensor pullback through that equivalence, with the canonical associativity isomorphisms; retain groupoids before removing automorphisms.

At y∈U_tri compare the completed local rings of S^□(r̄) and X_tri: the completion of the framed lifting space at r_y is its framed deformation ring, forgetting the regular triangulation is a closed immersion on deformations (N/ordered-representability), and X_tri is unibranch at y because the fibre of S^□(r̄) is connected. If also δ∈T_regⁿ, r is crystalline, the parameter is strictly dominant and the refinement is noncritical. proofSteps: Put A=E[ε]/ε². The underlying E-representation W_dR(D̃) is almost de Rham; apply the coefficient D_pdR equivalence without setting its nilpotent ν to zero.

At σ retain the original ν-stable filtration. At τ≠σ replace it by the one-jump filtration Fil^i=D_pdR(D̃)_τ for i≤−h_{τ,n} and Fil^i=0 otherwise. Its only graded piece is A-free, and it contains the original lattice filtration because h_{τ,n} is the ambient minimum.

Apply L/artinian-lattice to this filtration and M/gluing to the unchanged localized module. This produces the unique free A-Robba module containing D̃ with the specified localization and E-Sen spectrum. Uniqueness follows from the one-jump filtration off σ and, at σ, inclusion of lattices with the same elementary-divisor multiset.

The replacement commutes with finite coefficient tensor products and is exact on sequences using the same ambient cutoff. Thus pullback, pushout, Baer sums and scalar multiplication commute with it. Apply the same cutoff to filtration terms and quotients; their A-free graded pieces give saturation. Partial de Rhamness is ν=0 at the required embeddings, which this construction preserves.

nodes.statement: Let ρ be absolutely irreducible with NT-regular δ, and work in a neighbourhood U_v of its pseudorepresentation carrying a universal representation. nodes.title: A nontrianguline rank-two module has no (φ,Γ)-stable finite-dimensional subspace
nodes.statement: For K=Q_p and an absolutely irreducible two-dimensional E-representation V that is not trianguline, even after any finite extension of E, D_rig(V) contains no nonzero finite-dimensional E-subspace stable under both φ and Γ, and this persists after any finite extension of E. A φ-eigenvector alone is not claimed to span a Γ-stable line.

Colmez’s saturation lemma for a rank-one (φ,Γ)-submodule is requested from PG.7 (R6); nontriangulinity is meant after every finite extension of coefficients, as in Colmez’s definition.
proofSteps: Let X be a nonzero finite-dimensional subspace stable under φ and Γ. The operators φ and γ∈Γ commute with each other, so after a finite extension of E they have a common eigenvector x≠0 in X.
The Robba-span of x is a rank-one (φ,Γ)-submodule of D_rig(V); by Colmez’s saturation lemma (R6) it lies in a saturated rank-one (φ,Γ)-submodule, whose quotient has rank one.
This is a triangulation of D_rig(V) after a finite extension of E, contradicting nontriangulinity.
acceptance: Establish the stated result with the specified coefficient category, all functorial maps and no additional genericity or étaleness hypothesis.

nodes.statement: Under N/rank-two-nontrianguline, suppose the differential-equation supplier gives finite-dimensionality of ker P(∇)⊂D_rig(V) for every nonzero P∈E[X]. Then P(∇) is injective: ∇ commutes with φ and with Γ, so its kernel is a finite-dimensional subspace stable under φ and Γ, which vanishes by the preceding theorem. sourceIssues.printed: The slope inequality is written with the absolute value of δ′₁(ϖ_K)⋯δ′_i(ϖ_K) at least 1, and the induction step compares with indices j∈{i,…,n}.
sourceIssues.correction: The absolute value is at most 1 (valuation at least 0), which is the direction used in (2.13); the comparison is with j∈{i+1,…,n}.
sourceIssues.reason: Rank-one submodules of an étale (φ,Γ)-module have nonnegative slope, which is what (2.13) uses; for j=i the stated strict inequality would read val<0 and is not what the argument needs.

sourceIssues.printed: The text asserts D_{1,σ}=T_σ(D₁) with T_σ defined as in (2.7), that is, replacing the weights off σ by the module’s own lowest weight.
sourceIssues.correction: For D₁ the weights off σ must be replaced by the ambient lowest weight h_{τ,n}, not by D₁’s own lowest weight h_{τ,n−1}; the Hodge–Tate–Sen weights of D_{1,σ} stated in the preceding sentence are the correct ones. For C₁ the two cutoffs agree.
sourceIssues.reason: D_{1,σ} is the saturated submodule of D_σ, whose weights off σ are all h_{τ,n}; applying (2.7) to D₁ itself would give weights h_{τ,n−1} off σ.

All eight sources were fetched (hashes match the packet) and every node was checked at its locator: BHS19 §§3.1–4.3 and the introductory example, BHS17 Theorem 2.6 with proof, BHSsmooth17 §2.2–2.4, Ding25 §§2.1–2.4, NT21 §2.3.1, Proposition 2.15 and Remark 2.16, Colmez08 Lemma 3.2, Definitions 3.4 and 4.1 and Proposition 4.3, DLB17 Lemma 6.3 (arXiv and published), Ding19 Appendix A. Added G/refined-crystalline-space (BHSsmooth17 §2.2, Lemma 2.4, (2.9)), which G/companion-criterion needs. Every source match was rewritten to say what the locator states; the 98 tests were given protocol kinds; locators with nonexistent subsection numbers were fixed. E1–E16 confirmed (E7 reclassified as a misprint); E17–E20 added. Added the consumer contract for PadicHodgeParametersInLocallyAnalyticRepresentations TR1–TR5 and an ordering proposal (Layer N foundations before V). The suggested file now imports individual modules and elaborates with lean-check, admitted-proof warnings only. Gaps G1, G2 and requests R1–R9 remain open and are recorded honestly; R7 needs a routing decision because PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras is now upstream and builds no rigid spaces.
